claims.claim: Israel is the second most targeted country in the world by cyberattacks (according to Microsoft)
claims.verified_figure: Per MDDR 2026 country breakdown of observed cyber threat activity impacting Microsoft customers: US 25.5%, Israel 7.6% (2nd), Ukraine 4.8%, Taiwan 3.9%, UK 3.8%. US 25.5% confirmed verbatim on microsoft.com; Israel 7.6%/2nd from microsoft.com search-index snippet + 5+ independent secondary outlets.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 2nd worldwide, behind the US (i24 headline/sub-line); secondary outlets add 7.6% share
claims.note: Ranking is global, not a subset (not 'allies only' or 'ransomware only'): it is Microsoft's share of all observed cyber threat activity by targeted country. Caveats, not errors: the metric is Microsoft-customer telemetry, not a census of all cyberattacks worldwide, and the headline attributes it to Microsoft. Some secondary outlets (theyeshivaworld) frame it as 'state-linked' attacks with 210 Israel vs 531 US nation-state events - a separate metric; on the primary landing page the nation-state section only names Israel top in Middle East & Africa, and the 210/531 counts were not verified in the primary. Period wording differs across sources (landing page: Jan 2025-Jun 2026 for the US figure; secondary: Jan-Jun 2026 or Jul 2025-Jun 2026) - minor.

claims.claim: Israel ranks behind the United States (US is the most targeted country)
claims.verified_figure: US 25.5% of observed cyber threat activity impacting customers (verbatim on microsoft.com), the highest share; Israel 7.6%.
claims.note: US first place confirmed directly on Microsoft's own page; consistent across all secondary sources.

claims.claim: The finding comes from Microsoft's new annual report
claims.verified_figure: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026, published 2026-10-01, annual (7th edition), reporting period Jul 2025-Jun 2026.
claims.note: Attribution correct. No percentage appears in the headline or sub-line, so the 7.6% figure (and the 21% ransomware rise / 39% Iranian-actor share reported elsewhere) were not audited as claims of this headline; 21% and 39% were seen only in secondary sources, not in the fetched primary page.
